The sky as it would look from another star, built from the HYG catalogue (Hipparcos, Yale, Gliese): real positions, proper motions and brightnesses. Choose a destination to travel there. Epoch moves every star along its proper motion on a logarithmic scale, up to a billion years either way, following the Galactic epicycle approximation; ticks mark events, click one to jump. Planet hosts shows only stars with known planets (Open Exoplanet Catalogue, snapshot to 2023: 5077 confirmed planets in 3823 systems); the 515 hosts that are also in HYG move and evolve, the rest keep fixed positions. Planetary system (from a host's card) runs the orbits with their periods and eccentricities, and the habitable zone; semi-major axes missing from the catalogue come from Kepler's third law, unknown eccentricities are drawn circular and orbital phases are arbitrary. Click a planet in the system view to see it close up: its colours are hypothetical, set by Sudarsky et al. 2000 classes for giants, Rogers 2015 and Zeng et al. 2016 for rocky versus volatile-rich worlds, lava worlds above about 1000 K, and brown dwarfs by estimated Teff. Brown dwarfs lists hosts of companions of 13 to 80 MJup. Diagrams plots every companion with a measured radius: mass–radius with the Chen & Kipping relation, period–radius with the Neptunian desert of Mazeh et al. 2016, and insolation–radius with the habitable zone of the selected host. Galaxy shows the Galactic plane from the north in the frame of the spiral pattern (arms: Reid et al. 2019; bar: Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016) with the Sun's epicyclic orbit over ±1 Gyr. Age evolves the stars with SSE tracks, through giants, planetary nebulae, white dwarfs and supernovae. The HR panel shows the stars within 100 pc: faint dots are where they are today, coloured dots where they are after evolution. Chart is the all-sky oval, Dome the view from the star, Space the stars in 3D. Click a star for its card, double-click to go there.
